minutes.headline: PACC voted to send a warrant article to the November special town meeting restoring its capital line.
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee met remotely, approved the amended August minutes, and heard the manager's report on streaming problems, COVID expense reimbursement and a new story-time show. It reviewed finances, voted to submit a special town meeting warrant article for the capital line, and heard the chair's update on the TC Passios studio design. It set the next meeting for October 5, on Zoom.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to accept a special town meeting warrant article, as written, that transfers funds to the capital line of the PEG access enterprise fund.
The chair will sign the article, note that the committee approved it, and send it in before the September 29 deadline.
The article is needed because the FY21 capital line was left out of the annual meeting warrant.
The finance report showed August interest well below earlier receipts and a lower Comcast payment, which the committee said it should watch.
The committee will pick Zoom or in person each time it sets a meeting date, and expects to stay on Zoom for now.

why_it_matters: The public access channel's equipment money depends on this article, so Town Meeting voters will be asked to approve a transfer from the cable access enterprise fund's available funds to restore its capital line.
Falling interest and a lower Comcast payment squeeze the enterprise fund that pays for local cable access, and the budget cannot be re-budgeted mid-year to make up the gap.
watch_next: The warrant article's September 29 submission deadline, then the November special town meeting vote.
The committee's next meeting, set for October 5 on Zoom.
